We offer merchants an end-to-end payments solution that provides authorization and settlement capabilities, as well as instant access to funds and payouts. We also help merchants connect with their customers, process exchanges and returns, and manage risk. We enable consumers to engage in cross-border shopping and merchants to extend their global reach while reducing the complexity and friction involved in enabling cross-border trade.

added.description:
To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts.

Job Category

Software Engineering

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Engineering at Qualified

Engineering at Qualified is a high-ownership, high-velocity environment where engineers ship customer-facing product to real enterprises at scale. We're building at the frontier of AI + product: developing agentic software and

embedding AI directly into our platform, using modern toolchains and processes that help engineers move faster while staying focused on high-impact problem solving.

Following our acquisition by Salesforce, we continue to operate with the pace and ownership of a startup, backed by the distribution, resources, and long-term runway of a global enterprise. Engineers have true end-to-end ownership from idea to production: scoping, implementation, testing, deployment, monitoring, and iterative improvement based on real customer feedback.

You'll work alongside a high-talent-density team that cares deeply about craft, performance, reliability, and user experience, and that raises the bar through collaboration, code review, and strong engineering principles. You'll make architecture decisions, solve meaningful system design challenges, and see your work land quickly with customers, without layers of approvals slowing you down.

The Role

As an Engineer on the AI Core team, you'll operate as a technical leader who turns ambiguous, high-stakes AI problems into durable, high-quality systems, while raising the technical bar for the broader team. AI Core builds the retrieval systems and agent infrastructure that power how our AI agents find, trust, and use knowledge, and the developer tooling that lets engineers across the company ship production agents quickly and safely.

You'll lead significant initiatives end to end: faithful answering over a customer's own knowledge, retrieval that combines RAG and hybrid search, content lifecycle controls such as freshness, deduplication and source precedence, transcript processing, and the frameworks, registries, and evaluation tooling that make building a production agent a paved path. You'll partner closely with product, design, and engineering leadership to decide what we build, how we build it, and how we measure whether answers actually got better.

What You'll Do

Lead retrieval initiatives end to end: Design, build, and operate retrieval systems using RAG and hybrid search (lexical plus vector, reranking, filtering) so agents answer from the right content with the right amount of context. Own delivery from scope and design through launch, monitoring, and iteration.

Build developer tooling for production agents: Drive technical design for the frameworks and platform pieces our engineers use to build agents, including multi-agent orchestration, shared primitives for prompts, tools, tracing, and evaluation.

Own answer quality: Diagnose why answers are thin, wrong, or inconsistent by separating retrieval problems from generation problems (prompt, token budget, model choice). Set a quality bar we can test against, and lead the

work to reach it.

Design content and data models: Define how content from documents,

knowledge bases, and call transcripts is ingested, segmented, labeled, and retrieved, including the primitives behind freshness, dedupe, source

precedence, and internal versus external visibility.

Make AI changes safe to ship: Build evaluation, observability, and rollout

practices (offline evals, online monitoring, regression detection) so we can change prompts, models, and retrieval with confidence. Evaluate multiple

solution paths and know when to trust, redirect, or override model and agent output.

Set performance and scaling benchmarks across the platform we own:

Define and track targets for retrieval and indexing, LLM provider usage, and agent orchestration.

Own operational health: Ensure the reliability and performance of the systems your team owns. Participate in on-call, lead incident resolution for your area, and communicate clearly with the team and stakeholders during incidents.

Use agentic development to raise leverage: Use coding agents by default for implementation, testing, refactoring, and documentation while holding a high validation bar. Create reusable workflows, patterns, and tooling that raise the effectiveness of your team beyond your own output.

Partner across functions: Work with product, design, and engineering

leadership to shape roadmap, tradeoffs, and requirements, and to translate strategy into concrete execution plans.

Raise team effectiveness: Mentor engineers, give high-quality code review and technical guidance, and improve standards, tooling, and processes.

Who You Are

Proven experience shipping production AI or backend systems in a high ownership environment, with a recent focus on LLM-powered applications.

Expertise building retrieval systems using RAG and hybrid search, including chunking and indexing strategy, embeddings, vector and lexical search,

reranking, and measuring retrieval quality.

Expertise building developer tooling that lets developers build production agents, which can include frameworks for multi-agent orchestration, an agent and tool registry, and shared infrastructure for tracing and evaluation.

Experience owning platform initiatives from design through adoption,

across systems such as retrieval and indexing, LLM provider integrations, and agent orchestration, including driving adoption and evolving the platform as usage grows.

Demonstrated technical leadership: you lead significant projects, design solutions for non-trivial problems by weighing tradeoffs, and influence architecture and execution beyond your immediate workstream.

Strong track record delivering complex projects with multiple stakeholders, dependencies, or phases.

Strong backend engineering fundamentals and proficiency in languages such as Ruby on Rails, Python, JavaScript, or Go, with SQL and RDBMS experience (PostgreSQL preferred).

Hands-on experience with the AI application lifecycle: experiment setup, dataset curation, offline evaluation, error analysis, deployment, and online evaluation.

Comfortable operating in ambiguity and driving clarity: you can frame problems, propose solutions, and align others.

Strong communicator across functions, able to explain technical ideas to both technical and non-technical audiences and to translate complex concepts into business impact.

Ownership mindset and bias for action. You raise the bar for the team through mentoring, code review, and your own work.

Curious and continuously learning, with an agent-forward approach to how you build software.

Nice to Have

Experience with pgvector or other vector indexes, and with query performance at scale.

Experience with content ingestion from third-party systems (document stores, knowledge bases, CRM knowledge objects) and the lifecycle problems that follow: sync state, dedupe, source conflict.

Experience processing conversation or call transcripts, including handling PII and consent constraints.

Experience designing evaluation suites that score qualities such as thoroughness and faithfulness, not only correctness.

Experience with voice or real-time conversational agents.

Experience with enterprise SaaS (especially B2B marketing or sales tech) or Salesforce/CRM integrations.

Startup experience and rapid shipping.

Why Join Qualified

Foundational impact: Shape how our AI agents retrieve, reason, and answer, and the tooling every engineer here uses to build them.

Lead real initiatives: Own significant projects end to end, with scope and

influence that grow as you deliver. You'll own the platform as it scales, from retrieval to model providers to agent orchestration, and set the performance and reliability bar that grows with the company.

AI as a core product surface: Turn new AI capabilities into dependable

experiences that customers trust, with strong engineering around evaluation, observability, and iteration.

High bar, low bureaucracy: Work with a team that values craft and decisive execution, where strong ideas win and shipping is the default.

Room to grow: Take on larger technical and product scope over time: leading projects, influencing architecture, and leveling up quickly.

If you're excited to build retrieval systems and agent infrastructure at the intersection of AI and enterprise software, we'd love to hear from you.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world.

Accommodations

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application or the recruiting process, please submit a request via this Accommodations Request Form.

Please note that Salesforce uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help our recruiters assess and evaluate candidates’ resumes and qualifications throughout the recruiting process. Humans will always make any candidate selection and hiring decisions. Please see our Candidate Privacy Statement for more information about how we use your personal data and your rights, including with regard to use of AI tools and opt out options.

Posting Statement

Salesforce is an equal opportunity employer and maintains a policy of non-discrimination with all employees and applicants for employment. What does that mean exactly? It means that at Salesforce, we believe in equality for all. And we believe we can lead the path to equality in part by creating a workplace that’s inclusive, and free from discrimination. Know your rights: workplace discrimination is illegal. Any employee or potential employee will be assessed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications – without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender expression or identity, transgender status, age, disability, veteran or marital status, political viewpoint, or other classifications protected by law. This policy applies to current and prospective employees, no matter where they are in their Salesforce employment journey. It also applies to recruiting, hiring, job assignment, compensation, promotion, benefits, training, assessment of job performance, discipline, termination, and everything in between. Recruiting, hiring, and promotion decisions at Salesforce are fair and based on merit. The same goes for compensation, benefits, promotions, transfers, reduction in workforce, recall, training, and education.

In the United States, compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, job level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, and benefits. Salesforce offers a variety of benefits to help you live well including: time off programs, medical, dental, vision, mental health support, paid parental leave, life and disability insurance, 401(k), and an employee stock purchasing program. added.title: Site Reliability Engineer - Memphis
added.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.
SITE RELIABILITY ENGINEER

As a Site Reliability Engineer focused on campus reliability, you will design what the campus watches and trusts, technically command cross-discipline SEVs, and build the guardrails that make the next incident smaller. You are the connective tissue across compute, network, storage, power, and cooling on one of the largest AI training campuses in the world. This role demands calm incident leadership, fleet-scale observability judgment, and the ability to drive reliability work across software and facility boundaries. We are looking for candidates from power plants, nuclear power plants, data centers, or people who currently work or have worked in facilities like SpaceXSI with power, compute, cooling, and related plant systems.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Own monitoring architecture and signal quality across GPU and host telemetry (DCGM, Prometheus/Grafana) and facility telemetry (BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, CDU / direct liquid cooling): what we alert on, suppress, and trust. Consume NOC noise-disposition feedback to drive suppression and redesign. Treat alert noise as a design failure, not an operator failure
Provide SEV command support: technical incident leadership, bridge coordination with the NOC, paging and escalation (e.g., PagerDuty), and timeline and severity hygiene
Run blameless postmortems and drive corrective actions to closed, not filed
Gate high-risk change: fleet-scale firmware/BIOS/BMC rollouts (Redfish, canaries, rollback) and SOP/MOP/EOP-governed work on power and cooling systems through a disciplined change management process
Lead cross-functional reliability projects spanning compute, network (InfiniBand/RoCE), storage, and facility signal boundaries, including grey failures that cross those boundaries (e.g., NVLink flapping, thermal throttling, power sequencing)
Partner with Hardware Failure Analysis on systemic failure classes: turn fleet data (MTBF/AFR, repeat-RMA trends) into monitoring, stop-rules, and vendor RCA inputs
Build and maintain playbooks, run game days, and keep cross-discipline dependency maps current. Own runbook quality jointly with the NOC (SRE designs; NOC operates and corrects)
Define error budgets and availability objectives at campus and service boundaries as adopted by the business
Participate in on-call rotations and incident response for SEV-class events in the Memphis / Southaven data center campus
Demonstrate monitoring and observability design at fleet or campus scale, including alert hygiene, suppression, and signal quality
Treats alert noise as a design failure, not an operator failure
Improve mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to resolve (MTTR) for severity-class events, and ensure blameless postmortems with closed action items.
Increase the alert actionable ratio and reduce recurrence of incident classes.
Expand monitoring coverage of critical dependencies across compute, network, storage, power, and cooling.
Minimize GPU fleet availability lost to infrastructure events.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree in systems engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, or STEM discipline
5+ years of experience in site reliability, systems engineering, plant operations, or large-scale production operations
Experience with at least one of: Prometheus/Grafana, NVIDIA DCGM, or industrial telemetry and controls (SCADA, BMS/BAS, EPMS, DCIM, PLCs, Modbus/BACnet)
Experience working across at least two of: compute, network, storage, power, and cooling / facilities telemetry
Experience writing and operating playbooks, runbooks, or SOP/MOP/EOPs with a 24/7 operations, control room, or NOC partner
Experience with scripting (Python, Bash) for automation and analysis

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

General experience in at least one systems language (C, C++, Java, Go, Rust, or similar) – not required to be expert in all of them
Excellent problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to reliability engineering
Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams, including NOC, data center operations, hardware failure analysis, and infrastructure engineering
Proven large-scale incident command experience and calm technical leadership on a bridge, whether from an SRE/NOC bridge or a plant control room
Demonstrated monitoring and observability design at fleet or campus scale, including alert hygiene, suppression, and signal quality
Experience in power plants, nuclear power plants, high-performance computing, data center environments, or other high-consequence industrial control environments (ICS/OT)
Current or prior work in data centers or facilities like SpaceXSI spanning power, compute, cooling, and related plant systems, including CDU / direct liquid cooling
Experience in AI/ML infrastructure or supercomputing environments: GB200/NVL72 or H100/H200-class GPU fleets, NCCL, InfiniBand/RoCE, Slurm or Kubernetes
Fleet firmware and BMC management (Redfish, IPMI), including firmware release validation and staged rollouts
Reliability engineering methods: MTBF/AFR analysis, reliability-centered maintenance, grey-failure diagnosis, and vendor RCA/RMA partnership
Experience with CMMS (e.g., Maximo) and commissioning / integrated systems testing (IST) and operational turnover
Hands-on definition and use of SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets at service or campus boundaries
Experience running game days, dependency mapping, and closed-loop corrective action programs
Familiarity with data center hardware and plant signals (servers, GPUs, networking, power, cooling) in addition to software telemetry
Prior work in a fast-paced startup or tech company like SpaceXSI
Experience in power plants, nuclear power plants, data centers, or facilities like SpaceXSI — current or prior — spanning power, compute, cooling, or related plant systems
Proven large-scale incident command experience and calm technical leadership on a bridge; nuclear control-room, shift supervisor / Senior Reactor Operator (SRO), Shift Technical Advisor, or Navy nuclear experience counts as incident command
Cross-team facilitation and systems engineering depth across software and facility boundaries

Sr. Applied Machine Learning Engineer

Team:
Engineering

Onsite - Sawtelle (Between Santa Monica & West LA)

Head of Engineering

About Plug

Plug is an automotive fintech startup building the marketplace for electric vehicles. Consumers, dealers and commercial partners trade in, sell and auction used EVs on a platform built only for electric vehicles. Nothing in it is adapted from legacy automotive.

Consumers get an instant cash offer in minutes, backed by data-driven pricing and battery state-of-health analysis. Pickup, payment and title transfer are handled end to end. Franchise and independent dealers across the United States bid in real time on inventory sourced directly from these consumers, dealers and commercial partners. Sellers get a fast, fair exit, and dealers get a dedicated channel for sourcing used EV inventory.

Plug was founded in 2023 and is led by former Tesla executives. It is backed by a $20M Series A from Lightspeed Venture Partners. We're building the most AI-native startup team in Los Angeles: operators, engineers and ML researchers building the transaction rails for the fast-growing used EV market.

WHY PLUG

You'll help build the biggest infrastructure opportunity in automotive.
You'll work on a platform built only for EVs, with nothing adapted from legacy automotive.
You'll be part of an AI-native company that is rethinking how work gets done.
You'll work directly with operators who have scaled multi-billion-dollar businesses in automotive, EV and marketplaces.
You'll work alongside a small, senior team, with high autonomy and a direct line to company outcomes.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Every car on Plug starts with a number: what is this EV worth today, and what will a dealer pay for it tomorrow? Those numbers come from our models. They draw on auction results, market data, vehicle telematics and battery health. As volume grows, our models have to get more accurate, update faster, and be easier to trust and explain.

You'll join our Intelligence team and work alongside our ML engineer and data team, who built the models behind pricing and battery health. Together you'll take those models further: sharper price and volume forecasts, battery state-of-health models built from telematics, and LLM pipelines that pull structured data out of vehicle, title and inspection documents.

What You'll Do

Build and ship agents and multi-agent workflows for operations, dealers, and sellers: document extraction, inspection and title review, dealer and seller communication, and internal tooling.
Trace every agent so you can see each step, tool call, and decision. Use those traces to debug failures and turn them into new eval cases.
Write evals before and alongside each agent: build datasets from real cases, measure accuracy and failure modes, and gate changes to prompts, models, and tools on the results.
Make model and prompt decisions with data: compare options on accuracy, cost, and latency, and run upgrades when a model is deprecated or a cheaper one holds up.
Integrate agents with the services the team already owns, through clean APIs and tools. Work within the existing architecture and raise design concerns with the owning engineer instead of routing around them.
Ship full-stack when the job calls for it: the TypeScript and React screens where people review and correct agent output, and the backend endpoints behind them.
Help the rest of engineering adopt the same patterns. Build reusable tools, examples, and short write-ups that make the next agent faster to build.

What You'll Bring

5+ years of full-time industry software engineering, with a track record of shipping features to production and supporting them after launch.
Hands-on experience shipping LLM features to production: tool use, retrieval, and structured output.
Experience building evals and tracing for LLM systems: datasets drawn from real cases, automated scoring, and production traces you used to find and fix failures. We care less about which agent framework you used (e.g., Claude Agent SDK, LangChain Deep Agents) than how you knew it worked.
Strong TypeScript or Python, and comfort working across the stack: APIs, databases, and frontend when needed.
You work agent-first. You’ve built your own tooling around coding agents, such as skills, MCP servers, custom workflows, or evals.
You enjoy being part of a small team: pairing, reviewing each other’s work, sharing credit, and building inside systems other people designed. You can disagree, make your case, and then ship the agreed plan.
A habit of writing things down: short design notes, eval results, and runbooks that others can pick up.
High agency in an ambiguous, fast-moving startup. You find the most valuable workflow to automate and ship against it without waiting for a perfect spec.
BS in computer science, math, statistics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent experience.

Compensation And Benefits

$164,000 – $200,000

Salary ranges come from independent, third-party benchmarking against national compensation data. Where an offer falls within the range depends on relevant experience, specialized skills, training and qualifications, current business needs and market conditions. added.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About The Role:

CrowdStrike Falcon Host is a two-component security product. One component is a “sensor”: a driver installed on client machines that observes system activity and recognizes malicious behavior, then provides on-box prevention capability and remote telemetry to the Falcon Host cloud. The sensor processes thousands of events per second to provide deep visibility into operations on the endpoint, and performs rich correlation and computation to identify malicious events and blocks malicious activity.

The cloud component aggregates sensor telemetry for each customer’s network, correlates malicious behavior across multiple machines, and presents our customers’ operations teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.

This is a Sr. Software Development Engineer II
(SDE) role in the CTIO
team that is bringing multiple AI-based strategies together into an integrated capability on our next-generation sensor (lightweight agent) across macOS, Linux, and Windows platforms. The Sr. SDEs in the team own the design and development of the features that put AI on the endpoint: operationalizing machine learning models inside the sensor, building the data pipelines that collect, transform and deliver sensor telemetry for model training, evaluation and on-device inference, and integrating those capabilities with the core sensor features. Features will cross-cut most core OS subsystems such as file system, memory, process, and networking, and many are built with shared components across platforms. The team operates under the Agile development principles and ships frequently.

The CTIO
team at CrowdStrike is responsible for defining and executing the company's technology vision and strategy, driving innovation and overseeing the development and evolution of the Falcon platform. The CTIO ensures CrowdStrike maintains its position as a technology leader by fostering engineering excellence, aligning technical capabilities with business objectives, and anticipating emerging threats and market trends.

What You’ll Do:

Collaborate with all the sensor development teams, across the company, on architecture and strategic initiatives.
Conceptualize and develop new product features.
Provide guidance and support to development teams in designing and implementing software for cross-platform delivery (Windows, macOS, Linux).
Take ownership of features throughout the entire lifecycle, from initial design to final delivery, including presenting product demonstrations at the conclusion of each sprint.
Engage in cross-functional collaboration with teams situated in various locations.

What You’ll Need:

Deep knowledge of C/C++; Swift experience required for macOS-focused candidates; Windows OS Kernel and Driver Development experience required for Windows-focused candidates.
Hands-on experience operationalizing machine learning models on the endpoint, including building the data pipelines that collect, transform and deliver sensor telemetry for model training, evaluation and on-device inference.
Extensive, fundamental understanding of internals for your primary platform (macOS, Linux, or Windows)
Proven experience in debugging memory corruption issues, process contentions, and system performance bottlenecks.
Demonstrated experience collaborating with teams to successfully deliver major features and releases.
Ability to lead, mentor, communicate, collaborate, and operate effectively within a geographically distributed team.

added.description:
Who We Are

Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.

Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.

With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.

Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.

About The Role

Our software team is growing, and we are looking for talented engineers to join us and be instrumental to one of the following areas: Data Platform, Simulation, and Technical Infrastructure.

Data Platform: The Data Platform serves as a comprehensive management system for Nuro AI Driver's data, labels, and metrics, facilitating seamless access functionality. The team focuses on data annotation across various domains, including 2D/3D perception, mapping, behavior trajectory, and language/text. It also handles data ingestion and mining, employing methods such as heuristics and embedding search. Additionally, the platform supports the autonomy evaluation infrastructure by providing detailed introspection.
Simulation: The Simulation team builds the simulator that allows us to develop and test our autonomous driving technology in a virtual setting. We work on the core simulator and simulation frameworks, sensor simulation, scenario generation, and solutions that combine real-world data with synthetic techniques to push the boundaries of what can be simulated, collaborating closely with teams across Autonomy and AI Platform to allow us to simulate realistically and reliably at scale.
Technical Infrastructure: this group owns few fundamental services for entire engineering organizations: generic compute platform to host mission-critical workflows such as data processing and simulation, storage management service which manages hundreds of PB of data, cloud infrastructure serves as IaaC which provisions and maintains all cloud resources, engineering productivity provides tools such as build and CI/CD to make engineering work more efficient.

About You

You have deep expertise and prior experience in some or many of the following areas:

2+ years of relevant industry experience in addition to a Bachelor’s Degree, Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or related field.
Must have strong programming skills in Python, C++ or Go
You have experience in one or more of the following areas: large-scale distributed systems; data storage and processing systems; modern microservice architecture; machine learning, multithreading; x86 architecture; and software performance tuning and optimization, robotics software frameworks, different compute modalities (CPU, GPU, FPGA) etc.

At Nuro, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. For this position, the reasonably expected pay range is between $160,360 and $240,540 for the different levels at which this job has been scoped. Your base pay will depend on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, education, location, and skills. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for an annual performance bonus, equity, and a competitive benefits package.

To tackle such ambitious challenges, we need a team as unique as our vision — innovators who go beyond conventional methods and are eager to tackle tough, uncharted questions. We’re seeking individuals who challenge the status quo, dive into uncharted territory, and bring interdisciplinary expertise. Our team requires not only top AI talent but also exceptional software developers, engineers, product designers, field deployment experts, and communicators.

We are headquartered in always-sunny Mission Viejo (Irvine adjacent), Southern California and have US based and global teammates.

About Supermicro

Supermicro® is a Top Tier provider of advanced server, storage, and networking solutions for Data Center, Cloud Computing, Enterprise IT, Hadoop/ Big Data, Hyperscale, HPC and IoT/Embedded customers worldwide. We are the #5 fastest growing company among the Silicon Valley Top 50 technology firms. Our unprecedented global expansion has provided us with the opportunity to offer a large number of new positions to the technology community. We seek talented, passionate, and committed engineers, technologists, and business leaders to join us.

Job Summary

Supermicro is seeking an experienced Sr. Software Engineer - Switch Design to lead the design and development of high-performance networking software for our next-generation data center platforms. This role focuses on SONiC-based network operating systems and integration with leading networking ASICs (Broadcom, Marvell, etc.).

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Includes the following essential duties and responsibilities (other duties may also be assigned):

Design and optimize critical software modules, drivers, and APIs for high-performance forwarding and control planes.
Define the software architecture integrating SONiC with Supermicro’s hardware platform infrastructure to ensure scalability, reliability, and high availability.
Develop and maintain robust interfaces for telemetry, diagnostics, and system management.
Lead optimization of system performance, power efficiency, and resource utilization.
Provide technical leadership and mentorship to engineers across software, hardware, and QA teams.
Drive cross-functional collaboration with product, hardware, and platform teams to align on requirements and deliverables.
Engage with the open-source SONiC community - contribute upstream, review patches, and align development with community direction.
Evaluate and adopt emerging tools, technologies, and methodologies to accelerate development and testing cycles.

Qualifications

BS/MS in Computer Science, or related STEM field.
8+ years of software development experience in networking or system software.
Strong programming skills in C/C++ and/or Go.
Expertise in data structures, algorithms, and software design.
Solid understanding of L2/L3 networking in couple of the areas below:
Routing protocols: BGP, OSPF, EVPN, VXLAN
Control plane infrastructure: RIB, FIB, BFD, IPC, interface management
Layer 2 technologies: STP, PVST, MSTP
Network management protocols: AAA, DNS, DHCP, SNMP, sFlow, IPFIX, etc.
Experience with packet forwarding engines such as Broadcom (XGS), Marvell, VPP, or Linux kernel forwarding.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with SONiC network operating system development, integration, or deployment.
Familiarity with datacenter networking, RoCE, QoS, and telemetry frameworks.
Experience with open-source collaboration and contribution practices.

$185,000 - $205,000

In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, candidates may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as participation in bonus and equity award programs.
